nodes.name: Weekly Schedule
nodes.notes: Mondays 08:00 in the n8n instance time zone (set GENERIC_TIMEZONE, or edit this node). Each run reports the PREVIOUS Monday-Sunday (UTC dates).

nodes.name: Manual / Backfill Webhook
nodes.notes: POST {period_start, period_end, force?}. Replies once, at the end of the run. The schedule trigger has no caller, so scheduled runs just end (failures still alert).

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT (apart from the schedule). Data sources (DATA_SOURCES_JSON), service URLs, recipients, limits. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Report Layout
nodes.notes: EDIT ME for how the report looks: section titles and order, which fields show, labels, number formats, intro and footer text, extra CSS and the email wording. Data only; checked on every run. Values stay escaped and an incomplete report always says so.

nodes.name: Plan Run
nodes.notes: Checks auth (manual only), CONFIG including every data source, and the period. Scheduled runs compute the previous Monday-Sunday. run_id = report name + exact period, so a custom backfill can never collide with the weekly run.

nodes.name: Claim Run
nodes.notes: POST /reports/{run_id}/claim {ttl_seconds, force} -> {claimed, record:{status, delivered[]}}. ATOMIC: exactly one concurrent caller gets claimed:true. This replaces a read-then-write check, which lets two runs both pass.

nodes.name: Claim Verdict
nodes.notes: claimed -> carry on (possibly resuming a partial run). Already sent -> skip. Someone else is running it -> 409. Store unreachable -> stop (503): without the claim we cannot promise not to send twice.

nodes.name: Build Source Requests
nodes.notes: One item per data source from DATA_SOURCES_JSON, with ?start=&end= added to its URL.

nodes.name: Fetch Source
nodes.notes: Fetches every source, one after another. A source that fails continues as an error item, so one slow or dead source never stops the others.

nodes.name: Collect Sources
nodes.notes: Turns each reply into {available, data | detail}. "Unavailable" is kept strictly apart from "no activity" (an empty answer). All sources down, or a source marked required down, stops the run instead of emailing a hollow report.

nodes.name: Build Source Retry
nodes.notes: Second chance, only for sources that failed in a way that can be transient (network error, timeout, 5xx, 408, 429).

nodes.name: Fetch Source (retry)
nodes.notes: Same request as Fetch Source, for the failed sources only.

nodes.name: Merge Source Retry
nodes.notes: Replaces the failed results with the retry results and re-assesses completeness.

nodes.name: Render Report
nodes.notes: Turns each source's JSON into a table (key/value, rows of records, lists), with every value HTML-escaped so data can never inject markup. Builds the index.html file Gotenberg expects.

nodes.name: Render PDF (Gotenberg)
nodes.notes: POST multipart/form-data with one file part named "files" called index.html (Gotenberg's contract). NOT neverError: a 5xx must throw so the 3 retries really happen; a final failure continues down the failure path.

nodes.name: Check PDF
nodes.notes: Does not trust a 200: the bytes must start with %PDF before anything is archived or emailed.

nodes.name: Archive PDF
nodes.notes: POST /reports/{run_id}/archive (multipart: a "pdf" file part + fields) -> {archive_url}. Must be idempotent per run_id because it is retried (3 tries; not neverError so 5xx retries).

nodes.name: Check Archive
nodes.notes: Archive and delivery are separate concerns: an archive failure does NOT stop the emails. It is reported as a warning and alerted.

nodes.name: Fetch Subscribers
nodes.notes: GET /subscribers?report=NAME -> {emails:[...]}. Any failure or empty list falls back to FALLBACK_RECIPIENT_EMAIL.

nodes.name: Resolve Recipients
nodes.notes: Validates and de-duplicates addresses (case-insensitive), falls back if the list is unavailable, stops if there is nobody (or suspiciously many), and - when resuming a partially delivered run - skips people who already received the report.

nodes.name: Prepare Emails
nodes.notes: One item per recipient, each carrying the PDF (the binary is copied onto every item explicitly: it does not follow a fan-out by itself). The idempotency key lets the mail service drop a retry that already went out.

nodes.name: Send Report Email
nodes.notes: POST /send-with-attachment (multipart: to, subject, body, idempotency_key, attachment file). Runs once per recipient; each is isolated (a bad address becomes one failed result, never a failed batch) and transient failures get a second try.

nodes.name: Collect Sends
nodes.notes: Pairs each send result with its recipient. A bad address (4xx) is final; a network error, timeout, 5xx, 408 or 429 gets one more try.

nodes.name: Prepare Send Retry
nodes.notes: Only the recipients whose first attempt may have been a transient failure. Same idempotency key as before, so a mail service that actually did send the first time drops the duplicate.

nodes.name: Send Report Email (retry)
nodes.notes: Same request as Send Report Email, for the recipients that need a second try.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { status: $json.status, delivered: $json.delivered, failed: $json.failed, sent_at: $json.sent_at, archive_url: $('Check Archive').first().json.archive_url, detail: $json.failed_detail } }}

nodes.name: Record Outcome
nodes.notes: POST /reports/{run_id}/complete {status: sent|partial_failure|failed, delivered[], failed[], sent_at, archive_url, detail}. Only now is the run remembered as done. Retried 3 times.

nodes.name: Finalize Run
nodes.notes: Builds the final reply: status, counts, who failed, missing sections, archive link, warnings. Each problem also becomes one Slack message.

nodes.name: Fail Run
nodes.notes: Common exit for "no data", "PDF failed", "no recipients": releases the claim so a re-run is allowed.

nodes.name: Release Run
nodes.notes: Records the run as failed. A failed run can be claimed again, so fixing the problem and re-running just works (nothing was sent, so nothing is duplicated).

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.notes: The single reply node. Only manual / backfill runs reach it; a scheduled run has no caller, so it ends quietly (problems still alert).

nodes.name: Expand Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply (or at the end of a scheduled run). Returns nothing when there is nothing to say or no Slack webhook is configured.

nodes.name: Send Notification
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. Failure is ignored on purpose.

parameters.content:
## Scheduled Report Pipeline
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the backing services (a reference implementation is included: `node 06-scheduled-report-pipeline-mock-server.js`, port 4600): data sources, report store, subscriber list, mail sender, plus a Gotenberg (`docker run -p 3000:3000 gotenberg/gotenberg:8`) for real PDFs. The mock includes a Gotenberg stand-in.
2. Open **CONFIG**: edit `DATA_SOURCES_JSON` (your data sources: name, label, url, optional headers / required / timeout), the service URLs, `FALLBACK_RECIPIENT_EMAIL`, optional `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` and `REPORT_AUTH_TOKEN`.
3. Check the **Weekly Schedule** node (Mondays 08:00 in the instance time zone), then activate.
4. Backfill / re-run: `POST /webhook/reports/generate` with `{"period_start":"2026-09-21","period_end":"2026-09-27"}` (add `"force":true` to resend a period that was already sent).

**Each run:** claim the period (atomic) -> fetch sources -> render HTML -> PDF -> archive -> resolve recipients -> email each one -> record the outcome -> reply -> alert.
